Baalzebub
bā´ăl-zē´bŭb
n. (the god of Ekron, consulted by Ahaziah; in the Gospels, Beelzebub, the prince of the devils)
Hebrew baal zebub, lord of the fly. Whether the Philistines meant it as a title of power over plague-flies or Israel coined it in mockery, the Gospel form Beelzebub carries it forward as a name for Satan himself.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

“Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease” (2Ki 1:2). Elijah is sent to intercept them with a question: “Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron?” (2Ki 1:3), and to the king in person: “thou shalt not come down off that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die” (2Ki 1:16). In the Gospels the Pharisees use the name against Christ: “This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils” (Mat 12:24).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) treats Beelzebub as the name of the god of Ekron, and in the New Testament as a name of the prince of evil spirits.

expand to see more

BEELZEBUB, n. The god of flies, an idol of the Ekronites; in the New Testament, the prince of the devils.

ORACLE, n. Among the heathen, the answer of a god or some person reputed to be a god, to an inquiry made respecting some future event.

DIVINATION, n. The act of divining; a foretelling future events, or discovering things secret, by unlawful arts.

Key Scripture

2Ki 1:2 — "And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease."

2Ki 1:3 — "But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say unto them, Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron?"

2Ki 1:16 — "And he said unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Forasmuch as thou hast sent messengers to enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron, is it not because there is no God in Israel to enquire of his word? therefore thou shalt not come down off that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die."

Mat 12:24 — "But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils."

Modern Corruption

Elijah's question is the whole indictment: is it not because there is no God in Israel? The sin was where the king sent, not what he asked.

expand to see more

Ahaziah's question was reasonable enough — whether he would recover — and God answered it, through Elijah, in the negative. The sin was the address. Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron? The king of the covenant people, injured in his own house, sent past the prophet in his own land to a Philistine shrine. Saul had done the same at Endor and died the next day. Consulting the dead or the demons is treated in Scripture not merely as futile but as apostasy, because it declares that the LORD either cannot answer or will not.

The corruption to name is the traffic in guidance outside of God's word, from the frank occultism Deuteronomy 18 lists — divination, observing times, enchantment, witchcraft, consulting familiar spirits — to its softer modern forms, which are not less a search for a word from somewhere other than Scripture. Isaiah 8:19-20 gives both the practice and the standard: should not a people seek unto their God? for the living to the dead? To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew baal zebub, lord of the fly; Greek Beelzeboul (G954); Hebrew darash (H1875), to seek, enquire of.

expand to see more

Hebrew Baal zebub (H1176) — Baalzebub, god of Ekron; 2 Kings 1:2, 1:3, 1:6, 1:16.

Greek Beelzeboul (G954) — Beelzebub; Matthew 12:24, 10:25, Luke 11:15.

Hebrew darash (H1875) — to seek, enquire, consult; 2 Kings 1:2, Deuteronomy 18:11.

Hebrew Eqron (H6138) — Ekron, a Philistine city; 2 Kings 1:2, 1 Samuel 5:10.

Greek archon (G758) — prince, ruler; Matthew 12:24, John 12:31.

Usage

"“Go, enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron” — the king's message."

"“Is it not because there is not a God in Israel?” — Elijah's question."

"“By Beelzebub the prince of the devils” — the charge against Christ."
